title: Ramified finite quotient coefficient square is a pushout on sections
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, finite extensions $E,F$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, and an inclusion $i:E\to F$. Let $A=\mathcal O_E$ and $B=\mathcal O_F$ be their coefficient integer rings with chosen uniformizers $t,v$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Fix a scheme $W$, $e\ge1$, and the ramification identity $(t)B=(v^e)$ [def-pur-finite-compact-support-scalar-data]. For $n\ge0$, on each object $U$ of the small pro-etale site of $W$, the square with top map the constant coefficient inclusion $A(U)\to B(U)$ [def-pur-constant-scalar-tower-adjunction], bottom map the specified ramified finite quotient inclusion $(A/(t^{n+1}))(U)\to(B/(v^{e(n+1)}))(U)$, and vertical maps the constant-to-completion maps followed by the specified finite projections [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients], is a pushout in commutative rings. All four maps are the actual specified coefficient maps, not merely maps identified up to an unspecified isomorphism. This assertion has no module parameter and no module comparison witness.

proof.text: Write r=n+1. Taking powers of the ramification ideal equality gives map(A→B,(t^r))=(v^(er)). The limit-lift equation for the constant-to-completion cone identifies its finite projection with the actual constant quotient homomorphism. The ramified quotient lift makes the square commute.

The constant quotient A→A/(t^r) is surjective on every object: a set-theoretic section of the discrete quotient induces a section of the constant sheaf of sets, and constant ring sheaves commute with forgetting to sets. Its section kernel is generated by the constant section t^r. Indeed finite-limit preservation identifies the constant set of the discrete ideal (t^r) with the kernel set; the discrete surjection A→(t^r), a↦t^r a, has a set section and therefore lifts every section of that kernel. The same proof applies to B→B/(v^(er)).

The discrete equality of principal ideals writes the image of t^r as a multiple of v^(er) and conversely v^(er) as a multiple of that image. These identities on constant sections show that the section kernel of the target quotient is the ideal extended from the section kernel of the source quotient. Both vertical section maps are surjective, so the quotient ring universal property gives the claimed pushout, with the specified bottom homomorphism by commutativity. Empty objects give zero rings; r and er are positive, including n=0 and e=1.

theorem ramifiedQuotient_sectionPushout (W : Scheme.{u}) (e : ℕ)
    (he : PurCompactSupport.Ramification l E F i e) (hepos : 1 ≤ e) (n : ℕ) :
    let g := integralConstantToCompletionOfUniverses l E W ≫
      (adicLisseForget W).map
        (PurCompactSupport.projection l E (n + 1) (Nat.le_add_left 1 n) W)
    let p := integralConstantToCompletionOfUniverses l F W ≫
      (adicLisseForget W).map
        (PurCompactSupport.projection l F (e * (n + 1))
          (Nat.mul_pos hepos (Nat.le_add_left 1 n)) W)
    ∀ U : W.ProEtᵒᵖ, IsPushout ((constantMap l E F i W).hom.app U)
      (CommRingCat.ofHom (show ((constants l E).ring W).obj.obj U →+*
        ((PurCompactSupport.finite l E (n + 1) (Nat.le_add_left 1 n)).ring W).obj.obj U
        from (g.hom.app U).hom))
      (CommRingCat.ofHom (show ((constants l F).ring W).obj.obj U →+*
        ((PurCompactSupport.finite l F (e * (n + 1))
          (Nat.mul_pos hepos (Nat.le_add_left 1 n))).ring W).obj.obj U
        from (p.hom.app U).hom))
      (((PurCompactSupport.finiteChange l E F i e he hepos (n + 1)
        (Nat.le_add_left 1 n)).map W).hom.app U)
